description: Benchmark dataset for RAG pipeline testing — AI Academic Copilot

cases.question: When does the autumn semester begin?
cases.expected_answer: The autumn semester begins on 1 September 2025.
cases.expected_relevant_text: All first-year students must attend the mandatory orientation session.
cases.notes: Direct factual question about semester start

cases.question: When is the spring semester course registration deadline?
cases.expected_answer: The spring semester course registration deadline is 15 December 2025.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Spring semester course registration deadline

cases.question: When is the graduation application deadline?
cases.expected_answer: The graduation application deadline is 1 April 2026.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Graduation application deadline

cases.question: When is the study right renewal deadline?
cases.expected_answer: The study right renewal application deadline is 1 March 2026.
cases.expected_relevant_text: study right renewal deadline

cases.question: What important things happen in October for tutor teachers?
cases.expected_answer: In October, tutor teachers must conduct individual check-in meetings with all first-year students and document the meeting notes in the tutoring system.
cases.expected_relevant_text: October is the most important month for first-year student check-ins
cases.notes: Paraphrased question requiring semantic understanding of October activities

cases.question: What should a tutor do in January at the start of spring semester?
cases.expected_answer: In January, tutor teachers should review autumn semester results, update student progress data, schedule spring check-in meetings, and complete the mid-year progress review by January 15th.
cases.expected_relevant_text: January is the start of the spring semester

cases.question: When should students register for practical training?
cases.expected_answer: Students must register for practical training by 1 November 2025.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Practical Training registration

cases.question: When must bachelor thesis topics be submitted?
cases.expected_answer: Bachelor thesis topics must be submitted by 1 February 2026.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Bachelor Thesis topic submission

cases.question: What is a study right?
cases.expected_answer: A study right is the official permission granted to a student to pursue a degree at the university. Every student must have a valid study right to attend courses, complete examinations, and receive academic credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: A study right is the official permission granted to a student to pursue a degree

cases.question: How long does a study right last?
cases.expected_answer: The standard study right duration for a Bachelor's degree is seven years from the date of enrolment.
cases.expected_relevant_text: standard study right duration for a Bachelor's degree is seven (7) years

cases.question: What happens to a student whose study right has expired?
cases.expected_answer: If a study right expires, the student loses the right to attend courses and examinations, cannot receive new academic credits, but previously earned credits remain on their transcript. The student may reapply through normal admissions.
cases.expected_relevant_text: If a student's study right expires before they have completed their degree

cases.question: How many times can a student extend their study right?
cases.expected_answer: A student may apply for a maximum of two extensions to their study right, each for a maximum of one academic year.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Maximum of two (2) extensions may be granted per student

cases.question: What does a student need to do to get a study right extension?
cases.expected_answer: A student must contact their tutor teacher at least three months before their study right expires and provide a credible study plan showing how they will complete remaining credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: contact their tutor teacher at least three months before

cases.question: What does EXPIRES_SOON study right status mean?
cases.expected_answer: EXPIRES_SOON means the student's study right expires within 12 months. The student must contact their tutor teacher immediately.
cases.expected_relevant_text: EXPIRES_SOON - expires within 12 months

cases.question: A student has been extended twice and their right expires in 3 months. What are their options?
cases.expected_answer: Since the student has already received the maximum two extensions, they cannot apply for a third. They should contact their tutor teacher urgently and may need to consider reapplying for admission if they cannot graduate in time.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Students who have already received two extensions cannot apply for a third
cases.notes: Hard case requiring combining two pieces of information

cases.question: How many ECTS credits are needed to graduate?
cases.expected_answer: A Bachelor's degree requires 240 ECTS credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Bachelor's degree requires 240 ECTS credits

cases.question: How many ECTS should a student complete per year?
cases.expected_answer: Students are expected to complete 60 ECTS credits per academic year, which is 30 ECTS per semester.
cases.expected_relevant_text: expected to complete 60 ECTS credits per academic year

cases.question: How many credits should a student have by the end of semester 4?
cases.expected_answer: By the end of semester 4, a student should have completed 120 ECTS credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Semester 4 - 120 ECTS

cases.question: How many ECTS credits does practical training give?
cases.expected_answer: Practical training is worth 30 ECTS credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Practical Training - 30 credits

cases.question: What are the different course categories in the degree programme?
cases.expected_answer: The degree programme consists of Basic and Professional Studies (180 ECTS), Practical Training (30 ECTS), Bachelor's Thesis (15 ECTS), and Free choice/External studies (15 ECTS).
cases.expected_relevant_text: course categories

cases.question: How many credits are required before a student can start practical training?
cases.expected_answer: Students must have completed at least 90 ECTS credits before starting practical training.
cases.expected_relevant_text: completed at least 90 ECTS before starting practical training

cases.question: What is the minimum number of credits needed before writing the thesis?
cases.expected_answer: Students must have completed at least 150 ECTS credits before starting their Bachelor's Thesis.
cases.expected_relevant_text: completed at least 150 ECTS before starting the thesis

cases.question: How many credits is the Bachelor's thesis worth?
cases.expected_answer: The Bachelor's Thesis is worth 15 ECTS credits.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Bachelor's Thesis - 15 credits

cases.question: What does a student need to complete to graduate?
cases.expected_answer: To graduate, a student must complete all 240 ECTS credits including Basic and Professional Studies, Practical Training, and a Bachelor's Thesis, and submit a graduation application before the April 1st deadline.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Completion of all required course categories

cases.question: A student has 220 ECTS and is finishing their thesis. What steps remain before graduation?
cases.expected_answer: The student must complete the remaining 20 ECTS, finish and submit the Bachelor's Thesis, ensure their study right is valid, and submit a graduation application by April 1st.
cases.expected_relevant_text: graduation application
cases.notes: Complex scenario requiring combining multiple facts

cases.question: When should first-year check-in discussions happen?
cases.expected_answer: First-year check-in discussions should happen during October. Every first-year student must have an individual meeting with their tutor teacher during October.
cases.expected_relevant_text: October is the most important month for first-year student check-ins

cases.question: What topics should a tutor cover during an October first-year meeting?
cases.expected_answer: Topics should include how the student is finding their studies, course attendance, understanding of ECTS credits, study right expiry date, any personal challenges, and what support the student needs.
cases.expected_relevant_text: What to Discuss in October Meetings

cases.question: When should a tutor escalate a student case to student services?
cases.expected_answer: A tutor should escalate when a student has 0 credits after first semester, has not responded to 3 contact attempts, has a study right expiring in less than 6 months, is more than 40 ECTS behind, has failed the same course 3 times, or shows signs of personal crisis.
cases.expected_relevant_text: When to Escalate a Student Case

cases.question: How long does a tutor have to document a meeting after it happens?
cases.expected_answer: Meeting documentation must be stored in the tutoring system within 48 hours of each meeting.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Documentation must be stored in the tutoring system within 48 hours

cases.question: I have a student who hasn't replied to my 3 emails and has only 5 credits after 2 semesters. What should I do?
cases.expected_answer: This student meets two escalation criteria: no response after 3 contact attempts and significantly behind on ECTS progress. The tutor should immediately escalate the case to student services.
cases.expected_relevant_text: has not responded to 3 contact attempts

cases.question: What is plagiarism and what are the consequences?
cases.expected_answer: Plagiarism means presenting another person's work as your own without proper attribution. Consequences can include failure of the course, suspension, or expulsion from the university.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Plagiarism: presenting another person's work as your own

cases.question: What happens if a student misses more than 25% of contact teaching?
cases.expected_answer: Students who miss more than 25% of contact hours may be required to complete additional work to compensate for the absences.
cases.expected_relevant_text: miss more than 25% of contact hours

cases.question: What is the grading scale used at the university?
cases.expected_answer: Courses are graded on a scale of 1 to 5, where 5 is Excellent, 4 is Very Good, 3 is Good, 2 is Satisfactory, and 1 is Sufficient. Non-graded courses use PASS or FAIL.
cases.expected_relevant_text: grading scale

cases.question: What academic integrity violations are there besides plagiarism?
cases.expected_answer: Besides plagiarism, academic integrity violations include cheating (using unauthorized materials in exams), fabrication (inventing or falsifying data), and collusion (working with others on individual assessments).
cases.expected_relevant_text: academic integrity policy

cases.question: What support services are available for students with personal difficulties?
cases.expected_answer: Support services include counselling for mental health, financial guidance, disability support for learning difficulties, and international student support.
cases.expected_relevant_text: welfare support for students experiencing personal difficulties

cases.question: Where should I direct a student who needs help finding a practical training placement?
cases.expected_answer: Students should contact Career Services for help finding practical training placements. They should reach out at least three months before their intended start date.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Career Services office provides support for finding practical training placements

cases.question: Which office handles questions about studying abroad or exchange programmes?
cases.expected_answer: The International Office handles exchange student questions and provides international student support.
cases.expected_relevant_text: International Office - Exchange student questions

cases.question: What should a tutor remind students about in December?
cases.expected_answer: In December, tutors should remind students about the spring semester course registration deadline of December 15th, and conduct urgent meetings with at-risk students.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Spring Registration Deadline: December 15th

cases.question: A student missed the spring registration deadline. What are the consequences?
cases.expected_answer: Students who fail to register by the deadline may lose their place in courses for the spring semester. The tutor should help the student contact the relevant administration immediately.
cases.expected_relevant_text: fail to register may lose their place in courses

cases.question: How is practical training graded?
cases.expected_answer: Practical training is graded as PASS or FAIL, not on the numeric 1-5 scale.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Practical training is graded as PASS or FAIL

cases.question: How long must practical training last?
cases.expected_answer: Practical training must last a minimum of 5 months full-time or the equivalent part-time.
cases.expected_relevant_text: Minimum duration: 5 months full-time

cases.question: My student's enrollment permission is about to run out. What should I do?
cases.expected_answer: If the student's study right is expiring, the tutor should contact the student immediately and guide them to apply for an extension at least three months before expiry. The student must provide a credible study plan.

cases.question: A 3rd year student has only completed 60 credits. How far behind are they?
cases.expected_answer: By semester 6 (3rd year end), a student should have 180 ECTS. With only 60 credits they are 120 ECTS behind schedule, which is a critical situation requiring immediate tutor intervention.
